verdictReason: The estimator-overcount hypothesis is credible, but the six unsubmitted candidates cannot be causally classified as unnecessary from this trace. The candidate values are empirical point projections, not authoritative tokenizer measurements or conservative bounds, and the historical decision/completion relationship is inferred rather than request-identity-bound.
method: The production request projection is HELD FIXED. Exactly ONE accounting component is varied at a time. Production thresholds are NEVER changed to manufacture an effect; the ablations are computed analytically from the trace's own measured quantities.

hypotheses.statement: The estimator's fixed 3-chars-per-token divisor overcounts text that the provider tokenizer represents with more tokens per character.
hypotheses.evidence: Over the 107 inferred non-compacting pairs the session's own provider-reported usage implies 4.129 chars/token on the message payload (3.473 on the full wire bytes, CV 0.0732). The estimator bills 3.0. The resulting estimated/reported ratio is 1.497827 median.
hypotheses.note: This is the DOMINANT component. Its historical attribution remains INFERRED_CHRONOLOGICAL_PAIRING rather than authoritative same-request identity.

hypotheses.statement: The estimator counts serialization characters that are not equivalent to provider tokenization.
hypotheses.evidence: The serialized envelope (role/content/type framing, tool schemas) is counted in full — the production-seam suite asserts that the envelope exceeds the bare text length and that system prompt and tool schemas each add tokens. This inflates the numerator by roughly 5,700 tokens on every request in the session (the constant requestOverheadTokens, 5,691-5,697).
hypotheses.note: The overhead is ~5.8% of a typical candidate estimate. It is real, correctly attributed, and must NOT be removed — dropping it would under-count. A hypothetical removal changes four of six historical trigger decisions.

hypotheses.statement: ClineMM counts more result content than reaches the provider.
hypotheses.evidence: toolResultShortenedCount = 0 and toolResultOmittedCount = 0 on every request in the trace, and providerReady.providerRequestBytes tracks compaction_decision.apiMessagesJsonChars within ~1,000-4,000 bytes on every non-compacting request. The API-safe projection is NOT smaller than what the decision measured.
hypotheses.note: Consistent with the upstream v4.1.26 correction being already present in this fork.

hypotheses.statement: The reported inputTokens field is not the complete prompt-token count, or is transformed incorrectly.
hypotheses.evidence: The installed @ai-sdk/openai-compatible maps inputTokens.total = prompt_tokens (complete) and inputTokens.cacheRead = prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens (subset). ClineMM reads inputTokens.total. The session's internal consistency agrees: providerRequestBytes / inputTokens has CV 0.0732, whereas (inputTokens + cacheReadTokens) / providerRequestBytes has CV 0.2214 — adding the cached subset BREAKS the proportionality.
hypotheses.note: This ACT did NOT add cacheReadTokens to inputTokens; the quantities are not disjoint.

hypotheses.statement: The historical 1.5x discrepancy is partly or entirely a pairing artifact.
hypotheses.evidence: The production-seam suite proves that a synthetic decision candidate and the dispatched projection carry the SAME estimate when invoked over the same provider-visible input. It does not establish byte-identical identity for historical requests. The historical pairing METHOD was corrected (order-preserving rather than positional) and the median ratio moved only from 1.50415 to 1.497827.
hypotheses.note: The pairing correction matters, but the historical comparison remains INFERRED_CHRONOLOGICAL_PAIRING; the trace has no request identifier spanning decision, dispatch, and completion.

hypotheses.statement: The estimate is conservative by design and does not cause demonstrated harmful early compaction.
hypotheses.evidence: The conservatism is real by design (the source comment on CHARS_PER_TOKEN says it 'slightly over-counts vs the conventional 4'). Applying the session's observed 4.129 chars/token to the six candidates projects 71,830-76,488 tokens against a 103,680 trigger, but these are unsubmitted point projections rather than authoritative measurements or conservative bounds.
hypotheses.note: The bias is credible, but necessity of all six compactions is not established. A bounded calibration experiment is authorized; a production estimator change is not.

ablations.name: H1 — chars-per-token divisor
ablations.heldFixed: The production request projection, the trigger (103,680), the effective limit (115,200), the underestimate factor, the compaction strategy, the provider request contents.
ablations.verdict: DECISIVE PROJECTION — at the session's own observed rate (4.129), ZERO projected candidates would have compacted. This remains a point projection, not an authoritative measurement or conservative bound.

ablations.name: H2 — system/tool overhead
ablations.variable: The constant requestOverheadTokens (5,691-5,697) contributed by the system prompt and the tool declarations
ablations.note: Removing the overhead would lower each production estimate by ~5,692, to 98,850-105,261. Under that hypothetical ablation, FOUR of six decisions would no longer meet the 103,680 trigger. This is a decision-sensitivity result only; removing the overhead is unsafe because the system prompt and tool schemas do reach the provider.
ablations.verdict: DECISION-SENSITIVE BUT UNSAFE TO REMOVE — the overhead component changes four of six historical decisions, yet it is real provider payload.

ablations.name: H4 — cache interpretation
ablations.variable: Whether cacheReadTokens is added to inputTokens
ablations.note: Adding them would RAISE the reported complete prompt by the cached subset (up to +69,900 tokens at the session's peak), making the estimator look better by accident. It would also double-count, which the installed SDK contract forbids.
ablations.verdict: NOT APPLICABLE — the quantities are not disjoint. Rejected on contract grounds, not on effect.

necessityTest.required: current estimator >= configured trigger AND trusted actual input < configured trigger, for the SAME request content, model configuration and compaction policy. This evidence currently satisfies only the projection-based portion because historical request identity is inferred.
necessityTest.projectedActualInputAuthority: EMPIRICAL_POINT_PROJECTION derived from the session's own 107 measured provider usages; NOT an authoritative tokenizer measurement, conservative bound, or direct measurement of the unsubmitted candidate.
necessityTest.sameRequestContentAuthority: SYNTHETIC_PRODUCTION_SEAM only; historical request identity is INFERRED_CHRONOLOGICAL_PAIRING.
necessityTest.genuinelyOversizedEvidence: The production-seam suite asserts a genuinely oversized request still compacts, the underestimate factor still engages, the unknown-model-limit path still fails closed, and the final dispatch budget guard still rejects an over-ceiling request BEFORE dispatch.

conservationRequirements.unknownContextLimitFailClosed: PRESERVED — compaction.ts:439-444 returns undefined (no decision) when the effective limit is unknown in auto mode. Asserted GREEN in the production-seam suite.
conservationRequirements.underestimationProtection: PRESERVED — underestimateFactor still scales the budget down when the provider's previous count exceeds the estimate. Asserted GREEN.
conservationRequirements.providerOverflowRecovery: PRESERVED — overflow_recovery mode is untouched by this analysis and still forces compaction regardless of the estimate.
conservationRequirements.userConfiguredContextCeiling: PRESERVED — applyUserContextCeiling is untouched and can only reduce capacity.
conservationRequirements.systemToolOverhead: PRESERVED — must NOT be removed; it is real payload.
conservationRequirements.imageAwareAccounting: PRESERVED — the flat 1,600-per-image cost is untouched.
conservationRequirements.noChangeToProviderRequestContents: TRUE — the suspected issue is in the MEASUREMENT, not the request.
conservationRequirements.doNotTradePrematureCompactionForOverflow: A successor must not simply raise the divisor: the estimator must remain conservative on DENSE content, which is exactly what the underestimate factor exists for.

supportedCausalConclusion: H1 is the dominant credible source of estimator overcount. H2 is decision-sensitive in the historical arithmetic but must be retained because it is real provider payload. H3 is not supported. H4 is refuted by the installed provider contract. H5 is not excluded as a primary cause because historical request identity is inferred. H6 is not proven for this run: the six candidates support only an empirical point projection. Therefore the estimator-bias hypothesis is credible, while premature compaction of all six candidates is not proven.
